title: Certified simple connectivity of an audit model for Wuebben's proposed exotic S^2 x S^2 construction
description:
We define an explicit marked surface-bundle surgery manifold V_aud modeled on the data in Wuebben's proposed exotic S^2 x S^2 construction. Four hash-identified finite presentations are proved trivial by replayable derivation certificates, and separate geometric arguments identify those presentations with pi_1(V_aud). Consequently V_aud is simply connected. Comparison with Wuebben's fixed surgery member is isolated as a fourteen-clause Source Formalization D, with each clause tied to a target location, mechanical evidence, and its remaining non-mechanical content. The downstream manifold conclusions are conditional on that formalization and the cited classification, symplectic, and Floer-theoretic results. A reported contrary fundamental-group computation remains unreconciled; the paper lists all live failure locations without assigning the discrepancy in advance.

This deposit archives the complete verification artifact: the manuscript and its mathematical and computational supplement, the frozen presentations and sealed Tietze transport, every derivation certificate, the separately implemented Python and Ruby checkers with their negative controls, the certificate specification, the hash manifests, the dependency ledger, and the full run transcripts.

Replay has three levels. The certificate-only path reads frozen files and needs only standard Python and Ruby runtimes. The geometric-audit path recomputes the finite marked-fiber, torus, frontier, peripheral, and framing checks. The full reconstruction path additionally requires the locked GAP 4.11.1 and KBMAG 1.5.9 environment together with the proof-producing KBMAG patch.

Scope: the unconditional results concern the four hash-identified presentations and the explicitly defined audit manifold V_aud. Transfer to Wuebben's fixed member is conditional on Source Formalization D; the three downstream conclusions additionally depend on named external results. A reported contrary fundamental-group computation remains unreconciled and is disclosed without prejudging its source.
